purpose: Resolve the selected morning-afternoon return-profile concept into one exact no-value mechanism and challenge it against terminal and prospective families before any Campaign027 source partition, candidate value, comparison value, daily price, or forward return is opened.

selected_mechanism.name: intraday_morning_afternoon_return_profile_persistence_119p
selected_mechanism.formula: population PearsonCorr(r_am,k, r_pm,k) for k=1..119, where each vector contains adjacent log-close returns inside its own 120-bar trading half
selected_mechanism.economic_hypothesis: A higher value means the afternoon minute-return profile repeats the morning profile at matched within-half positions, consistent with persistent same-day information assimilation or recurring execution flow that may carry from the next open through the third close.
selected_mechanism.selected_bar_grid: exactly 240 one-minute closes at 09:31-11:30 and 13:01-15:00 after frozen timestamp normalization; standalone 09:30 is excluded and no return crosses lunch
selected_mechanism.return_rule: Form 119 adjacent natural-log close returns separately inside each 120-close half. The morning vector ends at 09:32 through 11:30 and the afternoon vector ends at 13:02 through 15:00.
selected_mechanism.pairing_rule: Pair morning and afternoon returns only by equal ordinal positions 1 through 119 within their respective halves. Use no shift, lag, lead, clock-duration weight, sign filter, magnitude filter, or market adjustment.
selected_mechanism.correlation_rule: Use equal-position-weight population Pearson correlation across all 119 paired returns.
selected_mechanism.zero_rule: Retain every exact-zero morning or afternoon return in its fixed paired position; never remove, bridge, replace, or tolerance-reclassify zero returns.
selected_mechanism.variance_rule: Require strictly positive population variance in both complete 119-return vectors.
selected_mechanism.bar_rule: All 240 selected closes must be finite and strictly positive before log returns are formed.
selected_mechanism.endpoint_rule: Only values within 1e-12 of -1 or +1 may be canonicalized to the exact endpoint; no statistical clipping is allowed.
selected_mechanism.missing_rule: Any invalid or nonpositive selected close, nonfinite return, nonpositive variance in either vector, nonfinite score, or score outside [-1,1] after endpoint canonicalization makes the stock-day missing.

overlap_challenges.reason: The terminal amount-profile factor correlates adjacent log1p(amount) values inside one 240-position sequence. Campaign027 reads no amount, uses close returns, and correlates two separate half-session vectors at matched ordinal positions.
The sign-run factor counts adjacent equal-sign return pairs and discards magnitude. Campaign027 retains signed magnitudes and has no adjacent sign-run count.

Those terminal mechanisms summarize variance allocation, bipower variation, return-magnitude concentration, or marginal third moments. Campaign027 measures cross-half positional covariance after separately centering both return vectors.

Campaign021 compares a stock with a leave-one-out market benchmark at opposite one-minute leads and lags. Campaign027 uses no market benchmark and compares only the same stock's morning and afternoon returns at matched positions.

Campaign026 conditions synchronous stock-market correlations on the sign of the market return. Campaign027 uses neither cross-stock information nor market-sign subsets and instead measures own-path repetition across the lunch-separated halves.

Those mechanisms measure net displacement relative to path length or the final close's range location. Campaign027 is invariant to adding a constant to either return vector after centering and does not use a terminal level statistic.

Candidate49 measures repeated close crossings of causal cumulative VWAP using close, volume, and amount. Campaign027 reads close only, contains no VWAP or crossing count, and remains historical-research-only.
Campaign027 contains one raw close-path statistic and no terminal factor value, transform, filter, model, or combination.
